document_read_extent.content: Complete author-hosted 16-page manuscript, including introduction, definitions, four main theorem sections, match-length applications, all proofs, acknowledgments and references. All pages rendered and reviewed because the text layer has font-mapping errors.

proofs_and_claims_examined: Stationary two-sided finite-alphabet process, recurrence R_n and waiting time W_n definitions; base-2 units, internal pp. 1-2.

Theorem 1: if c_n≥0 and Σ_n n·2^(−c_n)<∞, the recurrence product has an almost-sure upper bound and the recurrence product using the block probability conditioned on the infinite past has an almost-sure lower bound, internal p. 3.
Theorem 1 recurrence proof: Kac expectation for the upper tail and conditional block-probability counting plus Borel-Cantelli for the lower tail, internal pp. 8-9.

Corollary 1(c): choose c_n=εn and combine the two recurrence inequalities with unconditional and conditional Shannon-McMillan-Breiman limits to obtain n^(−1)log₂R_n→h almost surely for every finite-alphabet stationary ergodic source, internal pp. 3-4 and 8.
Match length L_m and exact event equivalence {R_n>m}={L_m≤n}, internal p. 6; entropy inversion stated there and locally proved in findings.md with positive-entropy and zero-entropy cases separated.
entries.extraction_check: PyMuPDF extracted text from all 16 pages, but embedded glyph mapping mangles symbols/formulas. The complete page-wise text is saved; all theorem displays and proof equations were checked against all 16 rendered original pages.
limitations: Finite alphabet and stationarity/ergodicity are essential stated hypotheses; this is not an unrestricted countable-alphabet theorem.
Source L_m permits overlapping candidate matches for short shifts; strictly nonoverlapping windows require separate statement or an explicit positive-entropy asymptotic comparison.
The source gives a match-length asymptotic, not a byte-level pointer/length code or universal finite-precision LZ77 coder complexity proof.
The source proof harmonic sum only needs at most one string per first-return distance, even though the printed sentence says exactly one.
